name: University of Amsterdam
summary: Research university in central Amsterdam; 23 English-taught bachelor's from psychology and economics to linguistics, four capped by numerus fixus.

ib.text: Full IB Diploma needed (IB courses alone are not accepted); English as an IB exam subject covers the English requirement. Strictest maths: AA HL at grade 4 (Actuarial Science, Business Analytics, Econometrics).

apply.via: Studielink, then UvA's SIS application portal

dates.label: Deadline if you want UvA Housing (non-selective programmes)

programmes.name: Actuarial Science
programmes.about: Mathematics, statistics and data science used to calculate and manage future risks such as fires, crises and bankruptcies and their financial impact, preparing you for insurance and beyond.
programmes.overview: Year one builds foundations in calculus, linear algebra, probability theory, microeconomics, macroeconomics, finance and programming in R and Python. Year two moves to life insurance mathematics, risk theory, machine learning for quantitative economics, econometrics and a research seminar. In the first semester of year three you can do an internship, study abroad or take a minor or electives, and the second brings specialised courses such as stochastic models in life insurance and the bachelor's thesis. A Dutch-start track and an English track cover the same content. Graduates are sought after in insurance and many other sectors, and can continue to a master's and then certification as an actuary.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Ancient Studies
programmes.about: The art, literature, philosophy, history and mythology of Greek and Roman antiquity and its neighbours, studied broadly across place and time, with material culture alongside texts.
programmes.overview: You study the history, literature, art, philosophy and material culture of the ancient world, from a wide geographical and time perspective. Year one includes Objects in Context, The Classical Canon and a cultural history of the ancient world; later courses cover Mediterranean cultural contact and religion in antiquity, with an excursion abroad in year two. You choose a specialisation in ancient history, archaeology, Ancient Near Eastern Studies including Akkadian, or Latin or Greek for Dutch speakers. The degree is shared with another Amsterdam university, so lecturers and classes come from both, and there is free space for a minor, internship or study abroad. A bachelor's thesis shows interdisciplinary analysis.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Archaeology
programmes.about: Past societies and why they matter today: materials, people and landscape, and how research is presented, with fieldwork internships in the Netherlands and the Mediterranean. Run with VU Amsterdam (ACASA).
programmes.overview: You study past societies and what they mean today, working with materials such as pottery, coins and bones, reconstructing landscapes, and learning digital recording and forensic methods. Year one includes What is Archaeology? and a first field school in excavation, and year two adds Science in Archaeology, Archaeology and the City and a second field school. Excavation projects run on Terschelling in the Netherlands and in Greece. Year three covers publishing excavation results and ends with a bachelor thesis, and there is free space for a minor, internship or study abroad. It is a joint degree with another Amsterdam university, with ties to the city archaeological service and the Allard Pierson Museum.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Business Administration
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus (650 English-track places): apply by 15 January; online selection test in February. Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL at grade 4.
programmes.about: Strategy, marketing, finance, management, international and digital business, with work on corporate social responsibility and the use of AI in business.
programmes.overview: You study how businesses are managed, covering strategy, marketing, finance, organisation, international business and digital business, with attention to social responsibility and AI. Year one is built on organisation, people, economics and methods, and year two adds marketing, finance and information management and a plan for starting your own business. In the first semester of year three you assemble your own route from an internship, study abroad, a minor or electives; the second brings a specialisation in accounting and control, entrepreneurship, finance, or the future of management and AI, and a thesis. Cases from real, international companies drive the teaching, in a Dutch-start or English track.
programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: 650 English-track places. Apply and sign up for the online test by 15 Jan 2027; the top 225 scorers get ranked places, the middle group is drawn by lottery.

programmes.name: Business Analytics
programmes.about: Analytics, AI, machine learning, programming and data-centred management used to solve real business problems, in a programme built around data.
programmes.overview: Mathematics, programming, AI and machine learning, and the use of big data in business sit at the centre. Year one covers calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics, learning programming from scratch, and opens with a course on real-life data cases. Year two adds machine learning, operations research, econometrics, and options such as HR analytics and an entrepreneurship hackathon. In year three you can do an internship, study abroad, a minor or electives, then take text retrieval and mining, marketing analytics and a thesis based on a data challenge. Ethics runs through the courses, including AI, privacy and cybersecurity, and graduates have direct access to the university's master's in Data Science and Business Analytics.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Computational Social Science
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL at grade 4; with AI SL you need an extra maths certificate.
programmes.about: Social science and data combined to solve real social problems: from day one you work for real clients on climate, health, inequality and AI, and present your results.
programmes.overview: You combine the social sciences with data skills, programming in Python, user experience design, web development, machine learning and responsible AI, to work on challenges such as climate change, health and inequality. Learning is project-based, with real clients setting weekly projects instead of exams. Each year has two semester-long courses: climate and digital surveillance in year one, health, mobility and inequality in year two, including network analysis and language processing. Year three is a capstone project with external partners, electives or a minor, and an internship or exchange semester. Weekly check-ins with tutors guide you.

needs.note: With Maths AI SL you need an extra maths certificate.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL at grade 4 is highly recommended, not required.
programmes.about: How people around the world live and make sense of their surroundings, studying culture, power and inequality around climate, technology and geopolitics, and doing your own fieldwork.
programmes.overview: You learn to study people through in-depth qualitative research and face-to-face fieldwork. Year one covers introductory anthropology, ethnographies and academic writing, research methods and current debates, and a mentor supports you throughout. In year two you take exploration courses such as Body and Culture or Power and Politics and a regional course, for example on Latin America or urban Africa, and practise ethnography with your own fieldwork and report. Year three has a thematic course in an area such as visual anthropology, plus career-focused courses. You have free electives for a minor, an internship or an exchange, and the programme is taught in English or a bilingual track.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Econometrics and Data Science
programmes.about: Programming mathematical and statistical models, applying them to real data and explaining the results, for questions such as how firms can grow profits sustainably. Start in English or in Dutch.
programmes.overview: Year one covers calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, economics, finance and Python, with introductions to econometrics in R and to data science. Year two adds advanced mathematics, machine learning for quantitative economics, econometrics, mathematical economics and a group empirical project. In year three the first semester is free for an internship, study abroad, a minor or electives, and the second combines a thesis with a specialisation: econometrics, on causal models and policy analysis, or data science, with language technologies and reinforcement learning. You learn to advise organisations on the impact of their strategies and to support decisions with data analysis. A Dutch-language track has the same content.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Economics and Business Economics
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus (850 English-track places): apply by 15 January; online selection test in February or March. Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL at grade 4.
programmes.about: A broad economics degree on the choices of people, firms and governments and their effects on society, combined with how companies are organised and run.
programmes.overview: Year one covers mathematics, principles of economics and business, accounting, microeconomics, macroeconomics, statistics and finance, and ends with a research project. In year two you study money and banking, econometrics, international finance and methodology, then choose a major: Economics, with game theory and advanced micro and macro, or Business Economics, with corporate law, strategy, accounting and finance. A research laboratory brings you into real projects. Year three starts with a semester of your choice, an internship, study abroad, a minor or electives, followed by a specialisation in accounting and control, finance or organisational economics for business economists, and a thesis.
programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: 850 English-track places. Apply and sign up for the online test by 15 Jan 2027; the top 300 scorers get ranked places, the middle group is drawn by lottery.

programmes.name: English Language and Culture
programmes.about: The literature, language and culture of the English-speaking world, taught entirely in English, tracing English from a language of Britain to a global one.
programmes.overview: The first year combines literature courses, from genres and theory to early modern and eighteenth-century texts, with linguistics, including the history of English, global varieties, phonology and grammar, and a course in rhetoric and writing. In years two and three you follow one of two tracks, World Literatures in English or English Linguistics and Literature, with restricted-choice courses and electives. Year three has three capstone seminars and a thesis. There is free space for a minor, internship or study abroad, and a scheme lets you spend the third year at a British or Irish university. The degree builds argument, presentation and research skills.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: European Studies
programmes.about: Europe's shifting borders, languages, institutions, traditions and populations, studied in central Amsterdam with up to 300 first-year students.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces Europe through its history, culture and politics, European integration and democracy, and European identities and cultures, alongside four language courses in a modern language chosen from about twenty, including Danish, German, Polish and Turkish. From year two you choose one of six majors: European Culture, History, East European Studies, Law, Politics or Economics, and take Philosophy of the Humanities. Space is left for programme-related electives, a minor or free electives, an internship and study abroad through Erasmus or global exchange, and the degree ends with a bachelor's thesis. Weekly workload averages around 42 hours.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Global Arts, Culture and Politics
programmes.about: Climate change, inequality and other big challenges seen through culture, politics and the arts, with four majors: human and artificial intelligence, curating the past, sustainability, or culture and social justice.
programmes.overview: Year one covers art and media, sustainability, cultural policy and AI, with courses such as Culture Wars, Historicising the Global and Fake News: Introducing the Human and AI. In year two you choose one of four majors: Curating the Past, Reimagining Sustainability, Culture and Social Justice, or The Human and Artificial Intelligence, and begin a thesis research lab. Skills courses teach academic writing, visual and digital literacy, archival research and interviewing. Year three brings electives, a minor and a thesis or final project, with internships possible in journalism, curating, theatre and research. Graduates work in museums, heritage institutions, archives and the wider cultural sector.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Global Communication Science (Communication Science)
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL at grade 4 is highly recommended, not required.
programmes.about: How media and digital platforms shape what people see and believe across cultures, and why what goes viral in one country may be banned in another.
programmes.overview: Year one covers global and comparative perspectives on communication, research basics, media innovations, crises and resilience, and a skills bootcamp. Year two deepens research methods, with statistics and qualitative approaches, and thematic courses on marketing and entertainment and on health and sustainability. A compulsory internship at an international organisation ends with an advisory report, which sets this programme apart. In year three there is room for electives, a minor such as Communication in the Digital Society, or an exchange semester, and complete an independent communication research project. Networking events and guest lectures prepare you for work in international organisations and communication.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Human Geography and Planning
programmes.about: How cities, towns and neighbourhoods work and how policy shapes daily life, from affordable housing to climate impacts, learned in small groups through research and practical plans.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces human geography and spatial planning, GIS, urban dynamics with Amsterdam as a case, and research methods, ending with a group project on the Amsterdam region. In year two you carry out a research project in the Netherlands and one abroad with one to two weeks of fieldwork, and choose thematic electives such as migration, development or environmental change. Three specialisations are available: Planning, Human Geography and Global Urbanism. Year three has a thesis based on your own data collection, with free space for a minor, research internship or a semester at one of the partner universities. Fieldwork with external clients builds practical skills.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Linguistics
programmes.about: The structure, acquisition and diversity of the world's languages; in year 1 you also learn a new language and compare it with those you already speak.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces linguistics, phonetics, morphology and sociolinguistics, with a language of your choice, such as Arabic, Czech, French, German, Spanish, Turkish or Sign Language of the Netherlands, and a research project on language acquisition. Year two covers phonology, syntax, semantics and pragmatics, analysis of an unfamiliar language, and courses on first language acquisition, psycholinguistics and neurolinguistics. In year three you tailor your studies through specialisation options, electives or a minor, with space for an internship or study abroad, and write a bachelor's thesis. Graduates go into academia, teaching, research and many fields where the analytical skills transfer.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Literary and Cultural Analysis (Literary Studies)
programmes.about: Literature alongside social media, art installations, political speeches and museums, analysed from an interdisciplinary angle to address the philosophical and social questions of our time.
programmes.overview: You learn to read literature, art and popular culture closely and to reflect on what they mean today. Year one covers poetic and visual analysis, discourse analysis and narratology, world literature, contemporary arts and media, and cultural memory. Year two adds literary and cultural theory, art, science and technology, and a case-study course, and in a Public Interventions assignment you design an unexpected situation in public space to study culture. Year three has a thesis workshop, current debates and a thesis, with electives such as Decolonial Thought or Moving Images Across Media. You have space for a minor, an internship or study abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Media and Culture
programmes.about: The global media landscape from animation and arthouse cinema to blockbusters, reality TV and AI-generated content, starting with a broad base in media history and theory.
programmes.overview: Year one covers media aesthetics, media theory, media research and the transformation of media culture, with courses called Doing Media Studies that build practical and creative skills. In years two and three you follow one of two tracks: Film Studies, on film history, theory and global cinema alongside filmmaking, or Television and Cross-Media Culture, on serial forms and digital platforms. Both include practice-based production in small groups, making a short film, documentary or television programme. Year three has space for electives, a minor, an internship or study abroad, and a thesis on a topic of your choice.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Media and Information
programmes.about: Critical study of information technologies from social media platforms to AI, preparing you for work where technology, information and culture meet.
programmes.overview: Year one covers media in everyday life, digital culture, algorithms and platforms, media theory and research, and practical problem-solving courses. In years two and three you choose a major: Cultural Information Studies, using data analysis, programming basics and computational humanities methods on archives, Wikipedia and social media, or New Media and Digital Culture, studying how digital media and AI shape society. You have space for electives, a minor or an internship in a media organisation, and study abroad is possible. The skills fit creative industries, journalism and administration.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Political Science
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus (345 English-track places): apply by 15 January; places go by unweighted lottery. Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL at 4 recommended.
programmes.about: Politics beyond governments and parties: how societies function and how to make an impact in communities and the world.
programmes.overview: The first phase covers a broad introduction: history of Europe, political thought, public policy and governance, international relations and law and politics, with attention to conflict, cooperation and power. In year two you choose one of five tracks: International Relations, Comparative Politics, Public Policy and Governance, Political Theory or Political Economy, and do a research project. Year three offers electives and a work placement, study abroad, minor or language study, and ends with an independent thesis. Placements have included the UN, EU embassies, think tanks and NGOs, and graduates go into policymaking, journalism and international organisations.
programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: 345 English-track places, allocated by an unweighted lottery among eligible applicants. Apply in Studielink by 15 Jan 2027.

programmes.name: Politics, Psychology, Law and Economics (PPLE)
programmes.ib: Selective: 34 IB points (6 subjects, excl. TOK/EE), Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL at 4; apply by 1 February, entrance exam 27 March 2027, then interview.
programmes.about: A small interdisciplinary college joining politics, psychology, law and economics to approach social problems from several angles and design new solutions.
programmes.overview: Politics, psychology, law and economics are combined so that you approach social challenges through all four lenses, in small tutorial groups. Year one has core courses in each discipline, such as Politics, Power and Governance, Law, Justice and Morality and Psychology and Society, plus integrative seminars on human rights and solidarity, and you pick a major by the end of the year. In years two and three about half your courses are in your major, politics, psychology, law, or economics and business, and half stay interdisciplinary, ending in a bachelor's thesis. You can add an exchange semester. Graduates go into policy, consultancy and research, or master's in law, economics, policy or psychology.
programmes.selectionNote: Selective: apply between 1 October and 1 February. Grades (34 IB points over six subjects), an entrance exam and an interview decide; intake about 250.

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus (300 English-track places): apply by 15 January; selection tests. Maths must be an exam subject; AA SL/HL or AI HL at 4 recommended.
programmes.about: How the mind and behaviour work, to help people with challenges at work, as consumers or in mental health, in small groups with mentor meetings in years 1 and 2.
programmes.overview: Year one covers all the subdisciplines, including neuropsychology, social, developmental, work and organisational and clinical psychology, cognitive neuroscience, research methods and statistics with practical training groups. In year two you learn to turn a psychological question into a study, then choose one of the majors: Work and Organisational Psychology, Psychological Methods, Brain and Cognition, Social Psychology, Clinical Psychology or Clinical Developmental Psychology. Year three starts with a bachelor's thesis and then lets you take a second major, a minor such as communication science or law, or an exchange. English and Dutch tracks share the content.

needs.note: Maths must be an exam subject; AA SL/HL or AI HL at 4 is recommended.

programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: 300 English-track places. Apply by 15 Jan 2027; ranked on selection tests of psychology knowledge, analytical thinking and study skills.

programmes.name: Sign Language Linguistics (Linguistics)
programmes.about: Sign languages from around the world: their structure, acquisition and use studied as a linguist, at one of the few universities with a full programme on visual-spatial languages.
programmes.overview: You study how sign languages are structured while learning Sign Language of the Netherlands yourself, over four levels in year one. First-year courses include introductions to linguistics and sign linguistics, transcription of sign languages, morphology and sociolinguistics. Years two and three cover the phonology, morphology, syntax, lexicon and psycholinguistics of sign languages, semantics and pragmatics, linguistic theories and research methods, ending in a bachelor's thesis. You have space for a minor, electives or study abroad, and internships are possible at the Dutch Sign Center, in hospital clinical linguistics or in research.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

programmes.name: Sociology
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL/HL or AI HL at grade 4 is highly recommended, not required.
programmes.about: How societies work and how social rules and inequality shape lives, across education, work, gender, class, media and politics, with research skills to improve society.
programmes.overview: Year one teaches sociological theory, research methodology, statistics, philosophy of social science and the sociology of institutions, with an Amsterdam Research Project in qualitative methods. Year two lets you explore six domains: urban society, race, gender and sexuality, migration and citizenship, globalising cultures, health and society, and education and work, with advanced statistics, theory and qualitative analysis. In year three you have elective space for specialising or a minor, an exchange or internship, and a Bachelor Research Project, an independent study within a group project that produces a thesis. English and bilingual tracks are offered.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May (earlier if you want UvA housing) and complete UvA Matching.

notes: EEA nationals with an IB Diploma applying to 15 English-taught humanities and social-science programmes skip the application file and €100 fee: IBO just sends your results by 31 August.
You must finish UvA Matching, a compulsory online programme check held in spring 2027, before you can enrol in a programme without selection.
You can register for at most two numerus fixus programmes in Studielink, and Political Science fills its English track by lottery, not grades.
